why: The answer makes a new array and copies data2 into it one element at a time, which is the right plan; but it writes data2.length(), which is wrong because length is a field, not a method, so the code does not compile. That makes this an L2 answer with an error.

concepts.quote: int[] copy = new int[data2.length()]; for (int i = 0; i < data2.length(); i++) copy[i] = data2[i];
concepts.why: It applies the copy pattern to data2 in the right order, but the code does not compile because it calls length() on an array.
It calls length() as if it were a method, but an array's size is the field data2.length, written without brackets.
It correctly uses new int[n] to make a separate array, but says nothing more about how creation works.

concepts.quote: for (int i = 0; i < data2.length(); i++) copy[i] = data2[i];
concepts.why: The loop visits every index from 0 to length-1 with the right < bound, but the bound is written with length().
The answer makes no claim about int.
The for loop is only used as part of the traversal, with no reasoning about the loop itself.
i++ is only used, with no claim about it.
The answer makes no claim about primitive types.
The answer gives no reasoning about init, test or update.
